- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5%.
- When sentiment shifts abruptly (e.g., from positive to negative), model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 3–7%.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model, apply a “sentiment-adjusted floor” — e.g., if sentiment <0.33, add 1–3% to forecast to avoid underestimation.
